title: Massing diagram (.arch.json), version 1
description: An isometric architecture diagram. Coordinates are integer cells on a ground grid: +x runs right-and-down on screen, +y runs left-and-down, and height rises straight up. A node's pos is its minimum corner, not its centre.

title.description: Diagram name; also the default file name.

background.description: Colour behind the diagram. Omit it to follow the viewer's theme (light or dark); name one and it is used in either theme.

groups.description: Flat zones drawn on the ground, such as a VPC or a subnet. Membership is by geometry: a node inside a zone's rectangle belongs to it.

texts.description: Free-form notes. Like everything else flat they lie on the ground by default, which reads as part of the scene rather than stuck on top of it; set `plane` to `screen` when a note must stay square to the viewer, or to a wall to stand it up.

images.description: Embedded pictures. The bytes live in the document as a data URL so the diagram remains a single self-contained file.

shapes.description: Flowchart shapes: flat outlines lying on the ground, for the parts of a picture that are steps rather than things. A shape is a connection endpoint like any block or zone, and a line into one stops on its silhouette rather than on its bounding box.

cells.description: Data structures: runs of slots — arrays, stacks, queues, matrices.

tabs.description: Several drawings in one file, shown as tabs. Use it for views of one system that do not belong in a single picture — an overview and a detail, a before and an after. A file with one drawing writes its collections at the top level instead and omits this entirely. The title and the canvas belong to the file, not to a tab.

name.description: What the tab is called. Name it after what it shows — "Overview", "Network detail" — since this is all anyone has to go on before clicking it.

shapes.description: Flowchart shapes: flat outlines lying on the ground, for the parts of a picture that are steps rather than things. A shape is a connection endpoint like any block or zone, and a line into one stops on its silhouette rather than on its bounding box.

cells.description: Data structures: runs of slots — arrays, stacks, queues, matrices.

id.description: Readable slug, unique across nodes, groups and edges in one document. Derive it from the label ("Web Server" -> "web-server"), never a UUID.

color.description: Lower-case six-digit hex. Omit to inherit the type's category colour.

type.description: Component type. An unrecognised value loads as a plain block rather than failing.

label.description: Caption under the block. Omit it to use the type's name; set it to "" for no caption at all.

pos.description: [x, y] of the block's minimum corner.

height.description: Vertical extent in cells, to one decimal place. The one measurement here that is not whole cells; footprints stay integral.

labelPlane.description: Where the block's caption sits. floor (the default) writes it on the ground in front of the block; screen floats it below the block facing the viewer; right/left write it onto one of the block's own faces.

group.description: Id of the innermost containing zone. The editor recomputes this from geometry, so it may be omitted.

props.description: Free-form annotations. Values must be scalars; `note` is shown in the inspector.

labelAlign.description: Which part of the caption lines up with what it names. On a block that is the block's own left edge, centre or right edge; on a connection it is which end of the caption is pinned to the midpoint.

kind.description: Controls the default colour and border style. Default "group".

label.description: Caption for the zone. Omit it to use the kind's name; set it to "" for no caption at all.

rect.description: [x, y, width, height] on the ground. Must enclose the nodes that belong to it.

labelPlane.description: Where the zone's caption sits. right (the default) stands it along the far upper-right edge, clear of the zone's contents; left does the same on the other edge; floor writes it on the ground just inside the zone; screen floats it above the top corner facing the viewer.

parent.description: Id of the enclosing zone. Cycles are broken on load.

placement.description: How a flat rectangle hangs in the isometric world. Shared by texts and images.

z.description: Elevation above the ground in cells.

plane.description: floor = lying on the ground (the default); screen = square to the viewer; right/left = standing against a wall. Content never renders mirrored, whatever the camera rotation.

spin.description: Rotation within the plane, in degrees.

behind.description: Draw underneath the blocks and zones, e.g. a floorplan backdrop.

src.description: A data: URL (what the editor writes, keeping the file self-contained) or any other image URL. An image with no src is dropped on load.

pos.description: [x, y] of the picture's anchor corner on the grid.

size.description: [width, height] in cells, measured within the plane. Default [6, 4].

text.description: The note itself. May contain \n for line breaks. A note that is only whitespace is dropped on load.

pos.description: [x, y] anchor on the grid. Which corner of the text this is depends on `align`.

from.description: Id of the source block or zone. An edge naming something that does not exist is dropped on load.

to.description: Id of the target block or zone.

label.description: Caption at the midpoint, e.g. a port number.

route.description: Which orthogonal family the elbow uses. "auto" picks whichever passes through fewer blocks.

bend.description: Where the run crosses over, as an x coordinate when route is "x" and a y coordinate when it is "y". Half-cell steps. Ignored unless route is set; omit it to keep the default corner.

labelPlane.description: Where the caption sits. floor (the default) writes it on the ground alongside the line; right/left stand it up above the line against a wall; screen floats it over the midpoint facing the viewer.

labelAlign.description: Which part of the caption lines up with what it names. On a block that is the block's own left edge, centre or right edge; on a connection it is which end of the caption is pinned to the midpoint.

kind.description: Which flowchart silhouette this step is drawn as. An unknown kind loads as a process, with a warning.

label.description: What the step says. The words are the step, so this is the content rather than a name.

pos.description: [x, y] of the shape's minimum corner on the grid.

size.description: [width, depth] of the bounding box in cells. Each kind supplies its own default.

height.description: How thick the slab is, in cells to one decimal place. The default stands the silhouette off the floor so its sides read; 0 draws it flat.

labelPlane.description: Which plane the caption hangs on. It lands on the shape's top face, so the default reads as writing on the slab; screen faces the viewer instead.

yes.description: Branch label for the affirmative answer. Only a decision has anywhere to put it.

no.description: Branch label for the negative answer.

yesAt.description: Which side of the decision the yes branch leaves from.

label.description: What the structure is called; written beside it.

description.description: A quieter second line under the name: what it holds, how big it is, what a slot means.

pos.description: [x, y] of the run's minimum corner.

rows.description: 1 for an array or a queue; more for a matrix. A stack is one column.

slot.description: One slot's footprint in cells. Default [2, 2].

items.description: Values, row-major. May be shorter than the grid.

ends.description: What the two ends are called, e.g. ["Front", "Back"]. Written beyond the ends rather than over a slot.

flow.description: Which way things travel through the run; drawn as a mark beyond each end.

marks.description: Pointers into the run, each naming a slot by index so it cannot drift off it.

link.description: Where clicking this element leads. Three forms: "#element-id" moves the view to another element in this file, flying the camera to it; "tab:Name" opens another drawing (by its name, or by its number when no name matches); anything else is a web address, which opens in a new tab after asking. Only http, https and mailto are ever opened. A click follows a link while presenting; Ctrl-click does while editing.
